name: CLARE, the Hon. Jason Dean

headline.note: The frozen official timeline identifies one potentially countable private-sector role at Transurban, but only at year precision and without evidence of substantive full-time status. Political staff, party activity, study and elected office are excluded. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.role: Bachelor of Arts (Honours) and Bachelor of Laws student
career_spells.evidence_note: Current and secondary biographies identify both degrees but do not publish enrolment or completion dates, load, or concurrent employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: A secondary synthesis with cited sources records ten years as branch secretary from 1992 to 2002. Pay, hours, exact dates and overlap with study and political-staff work are unresolved; the role is not assumed to be paid employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Party activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Office of NSW Police Minister and Leader of the House Paul Whelan (payroll entity unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official parliamentary occupation extract records this role from 1995 to 1999. Exact appointment dates, payroll entity, hours, leave and overlap with study or party activity are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Office of NSW Premier Bob Carr (payroll entity unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official extract records 1999–2003, and Clare's current biography corroborates service as senior adviser to Premier Bob Carr. Exact appointment dates, payroll entity, hours, leave and the transition from the Whelan office are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official occupation extract gives the employer, title and 2003–2007 boundaries; Clare's current biography corroborates the role. Transurban's current corporate page identifies it as an ASX-listed company, supporting private control. Exact start/end dates, hours, leave and campaign transition are unresolved; the managerial title is not treated as proof of full-time work.
career_spells.counting_note: Private control is supported, but year-only boundaries and unproven substantive full-time status do not support an exact headline duration.

career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary reporting records that Clare won Labor preselection in May 2007, and the frozen roster records the start of House service on 24 November 2007. Exact preselection day, campaign work dates, pay, hours and overlap with Transurban are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party and campaign activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster establishes House service from 24 November 2007. Clare's current site corroborates representation since 2007, and the Australian Government ministerial profile confirms his current Education portfolio. Ministerial and shadow roles are nested within elected service rather than recorded as separate employment spells.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

research_notes: The frozen official occupation extract supplies a continuous year-level sequence from 1995 to parliamentary entry, but does not establish exact transitions or working hours.
Transurban's ASX listing supports private control; a senior corporate title does not prove substantive full-time work.
The 1992–2002 party branch role overlaps study and political-staff employment and is not assumed to have been paid.
Ministerial offices held as an MP are treated as duties nested within elected office.
